<!-- pr-reviewer: fb37cf265bc70f5942b7e9a54f58b7aa6e83d46d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Reviewed at the safety tier, because this changes the stroke bands the post gate uses to refuse or allow posted G-code.

### What looks good
- The change is data only: three `travel` bands in `assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`. It brings the DNM 5700 in line with the travel rule in `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (lines 144-152, #457), which `vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and the Tormach files already follow. The figures (1020/570/510 mm) are the file's own catalog statement in `general.description` (from #614). No new figure was invented.
- It leaves the A axis's `nose_to_axis` unstated rather than guessing one, and files that gap as #1433. The first pin asserts that this is the only refusal left, so a new refusal would make the pin fail.
- The pins are well shaped: the exact bands, a clean `check_document`, no "the stroke is" problem at the gate, a 520 mm clearance refused by name, and `post_setup` failing on that over-travel.
- Commit subject, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1410`, the decision file `docs/decisions/1410-dnm-travel.md`, and the provenance line on the suite are all present. No process files, snapshots, goldens, `CHANGELOG.md`, build scripts or dependencies are touched.

### Safety reading (how the new bands are interpreted)
- The limit check reads `(w - origin[k]) * direction.sign()` against the band (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:352`). That is program coordinates relative to the work origin, not the machine frame. So the old Z band `-510..0` refused every move above G54 Z0. That was a false refusal, not a safety margin.
- **Is a symmetric ±stroke conservative or permissive?** It is permissive, by design. For a real WCS at machine offset `o`, the true legal band is `[m_min - o, m_max - o]`, which is L wide. The stated band `-L..L` is 2L wide. It is the tightest band that never refuses a program legal for some WCS placement. So it catches only moves that no WCS could make legal (|Δ| > L), and it can pass up to L of real over-travel in one direction. That is the documented law, not a new hole from this PR. A tighter check would need the setup's work offset in machine coordinates, which the file cannot know. The control's soft limits remain the backstop for an over-travel the band cannot see.
- **Compared with main:** Z max goes from 0 to +510 (fixes the false refusal); Z min stays -510. X and Y loosen from the half strokes ±510/±285 to ±1020/±570. The half strokes were exact only for a WCS at table centre, and they falsely refused corner-origin programs past half the table.
- **Other consumers of the same bands** (checked, no new risk):
  - `fixture::table_of` (`crates/app/src/fixture.rs:116-133`) puts the table top at the Z band's min. That is still -510, so the table collision box keeps its height. It gets wider in X and Y, which is the conservative direction for an obstacle.
  - The link router's ceiling (`crates/app/src/operation/job.rs:333-337`, `fixture_route.rs:201`) moves from WCS Z0 to WCS Z+510. That matches the stroke the post gate now allows, so the router and the gate agree.
  - `safe_retract: 0.0` (machine frame) is unchanged.

### Local results (trial merge with upstream/main af711f4: clean, no conflicts; macOS, sccache)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | green: post `doosan_dnm_post` 9/9, `probe_spindle_stop` 2/2; app `conformance` 7/7, `doosan_dnm_a_state` 2/2, `post_cycle_feed_spindle` 8/8, `post_spindle_rule_all` 5/5, `post_unit_word` 5/5, `probe_no_coolant` 5/5, `program_units` 7/7, `vmc_stroke` 4/4 |
| Other suites that load the DNM | app `machine` 33/33, `fourth_axis_pose` 9/9, `coolant_air` 4/4, `rotary_feed_cap` 11/11; post `script_doosan_dnm` 11/11, `cycle_hop` 7/7 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutation check** (the rule for new limit fields: each line must have a test that fails when it is deleted). Each mutation was run alone against `vmc_stroke`:
| Mutation of `doosan-dnm.mch` | `..._dnm_passes_the_stroke` | `..._dnm_column_still_refuses_by_name` |
|---|---|---|
| X back to ±510 | FAILED | ok |
| Y back to ±285 | FAILED | ok |
| Z back to -510..0 | FAILED | FAILED |
| Z loosened to -510..600 | FAILED | FAILED |
| Z `travel` deleted | FAILED | FAILED |

Every stated figure is pinned, and loosening the Z band past its stroke is caught by both pins.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Not verified here: the 1020/570/510 mm strokes come from the file's own description (#614). I did not re-check them against the DN Solutions catalog. Under the ±L rule, any error in L carries straight into how much over-travel the band can let through.
2. A follow-up worth considering, if one is not already filed: judge the stroke against the setup's stated work offset in machine coordinates when the user gives one. That would turn the ±L gate into the exact band. This is a design question for the travel law as a whole, not for this PR.
3. #1439 is stacked on this branch. Retarget it to `main` before this PR merges (AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack").

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
